question.problem: What are the solutions of the equation $2y^2 + 9 = 0?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, as follows:

$$
\eqalign{
		2y^2 + 9 &= 0 \[5pt]

		2y^2 &= -9\[5pt]

y^2 & = -\dfrac{9}{2}
}
$$

By taking square root, we obtain

$$
y = \pm \sqrt{-\dfrac{9}{2}}.
$$

We now rewrite $y$ using the imaginary unit $\textrm{i}=\sqrt{-1}\, \mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\pm \sqrt{-\frac{9}{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{9}{2}\cdot (-1)} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{9}{2}}\cdot \sqrt{-1} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{9}}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{-1} \\  & =\pm \frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we rationalize the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\pm \frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}\text{i} \\  & =\pm \frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{-1} \\  & =\pm \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $y=\pm \dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{2} \textrm{i}.$
